newsitem.title: UK: Sales of canned foods increase in Spain, Canada.
newsitem.headline: Sales of canned foods increase in Spain, Canada.

text.p: Sales of canned goods in Spain and Canada grew at double-digit rates from 1992 to 1996, while sales fell in the UK, Germany and France, a market research group said on Wednesday.

Measured by monetary volume, sales of canned foods rose by 16 percent in Spain from 1992 to 1996 and by 19.5 percent in Canada. Declining volumes and intense price competition led to value declines in Britain, France and Germany, research group Euromonitor said.

Vegetables remain the key sector for canned goods, accounting for 75.6 percent of the Italian market in 1996. The U.S. market is dominated by soups and sauces and vegetables, together accounting for 62 percent of the 1996 market, Euromonitor said.
In Japan, on the other hand, fruit and desserts are the canned foods leader, representing 34.6 percent of the 1996 market, Euromonitor said.
